recommendations.rationale: Single execution with no closed-loop counterfactual replay and a recorded no-change decision: a passing terminal reach coexists with a failing sampled holding, and the computation records show per-update solves far exceeding the control period, but nothing retained isolates a dominant cause. Controller weights are outside this phase's physical grant and no further candidate is authorized, so no parameter value is proposed.

Locating the update at which tip error and tip speed stopped decreasing inside the 0.05 s window requires per-update warm plans and optimizer iteration traces, which are not retained (source.historical_full_plans, retained=false). Deferred until such retention exists.

Testing whether the computation overrun and warm-start-dominated plan selection are causally connected to the holding failure would need a closed-loop counterfactual replay or causal-identification capability, which does not exist here. attribution.reason: A mean update wall time of 17.303696897140306 s against a 0.01 s control period, 35 deadline misses and a stopping-count split of Solve_Succeeded 1 versus User_Requested_Stop 34 are consistent with control inputs being carried over rather than recomputed at each 10 ms step, and sampled effective horizons of 9 and 2 (against a sampled 10) are consistent with shortened plans. This is a single execution with no closed-loop counterfactual replay, so it is a candidate relationship, not an established cause.

29 of 35 updates are recorded as initialization_selected (6 noninitialization_selected), and sampled accepted plans carry User_Requested_Stop solver statuses with returned constraint violations of order 1e-4 to 1.3e-2 and projection residuals of ~0.78 to 2.43 rad/m. The retained records do not show which selection behaviour fixed the late-window motion, and historical warm plans and optimizer iteration traces are not retained.

Reach and holding judge different quantities on the same run: reach is decided on terminal position error at the final time (0.00764 m, inside the 0.01 m limit), whereas sampled holding is decided jointly on maximum error and maximum speed over a 0.05 s window, where late_max_error_m 0.0581 m exceeds the 0.01 m limit and the late-window speed exceeds the 0.02 m/s limit, with residual terminal speed 0.6352 m/s. Both window criteria are exceeded, so this is a transient excursion, not a speed-only failure; the retained records do not localize the update that left the tip moving.

reach_passed=true with terminal_error_m 0.00764 m below the 0.01 m limit, so a reach-tolerance violation is not the failing criterion. This does not establish the cause of the separate window failure.

The retained comparisons are matched next-timestamp, single-step projected-versus-backend endpoint checks over one 0.01 s control interval with an explicitly recorded scope; a 10 ms projected-model probe cannot account for the whole 0.05 s holding window, and no causal-identification capability is available.

The improvement feedback records force_bound_violation_n 0.0 and per-tendon applied-tension maxima at or below about 7.99 N against the 8 N per-tendon limits, so no tendon force limit was exceeded and saturation does not explain the holding failure. These scalars are handed-over feedback without fact_catalog handles in this context.

The sealed feedback reports evaluation_validity 'valid', valid_complete_execution true, task_accepted true and solver_error_count 0, so the run completed and was evaluated; the holding failure is a criterion outcome, not a workflow or evaluation failure.

facts.statement: Sealed feedback for execution 4e358bd36ab54be3afd5003f36ff8110 reports reach_passed=true with terminal_error_m 0.007642608585867386 m, inside the settling position limit of 0.01 m, while terminal_speed_m_s is 0.6351726092425104 m/s against a settling speed limit of 0.02 m/s; the recorded terminal position [0.2826142589887697, 0.03368252098773442, 0.1885424181792968] m matches the displayed final-window position sample.

The same feedback reports sampled_settling_passed=false over a 0.05 s window: late_max_error_m 0.05813810428573256 m exceeds the 0.01 m position limit and the late-window maximum speed is reported above the 0.02 m/s speed limit (that maximum, 1.5810152739742807 m/s, is handed over in the feedback but has no fact_catalog handle in this context). The displayed final-window sample late_motion[0].error_m equals 0.05813810428573256 m, matching late_max_error_m, so the window exceeded both the position and the speed criterion even though terminal error at the final time lies inside the position limit.

Computation records for the run show mean_update_s 17.303696897140306 s against control_period_s 0.01 s, deadline_misses 35, stopping_counts Solve_Succeeded 1, initialization_selected 29, and 35 total updates, i.e. the recorded per-update computation time is about three orders of magnitude larger than the control period it must fit (qualitative reading of the two handle-backed quantities; no derived projection is claimed).

Sampled per-update records show effective_horizon values of 9 (update 26), 2 (update 33), 7 (update 28) and 10 (update 15) control intervals, optimization_raw_status 'User_Requested_Stop' at sampled updates (e.g. update 33), selection.plan_accepted=true despite that status (e.g. update 26), returned_constraint_violation 0.012896929259021382 at update 26, and projection_residual_rad_m 2.347088656497748 rad/m at update 26.

A sampled applied-tension record (aligned interval 3, update 31) is [7.943862879127355, 5.618626122659633, 5.253734658180846e-05, 2.244147411100176e-06, 4.169299444324358, 6.09025479283383] N, whose largest component is 7.943862879127355 N on tendon 0; the per-tendon force limit of 8 N and the reported force-bound violation of 0.0 N come from the inventory/feedback handoff and have no catalog handle here.

limitations: Single execution: retained records and model comparisons support candidate relationships only and do not establish a dominant cause; the feedback itself notes that a single execution and model comparisons do not establish a dominant cause.

The retained improvement feedback records a deferral: decision disposition 'defer' with status 'no_change_selected', an empty change set and execution null. No closed-loop counterfactual replay or causal-attribution capability exists, so the relationship between the computation/plan-selection records and the holding failure cannot be tested here; no further candidate build or saved-state numerical check is authorized in this phase.
recommended_actions: Keep the no-parameter-change disposition: the improvement decision deferred (no_change_selected, empty change set, execution null), and with no further candidate or saved-state check authorized here, no executable geometry or parameter follow-up is proposed.

If a future phase grants controller-side scope, the terms that bear directly on the holding-window criterion would be the holding/terminal tip-speed weighting and the solver-return/effective-horizon budget (advisory directions to test, not executed actions).

If retention is later expanded, retaining control_snapshots.json (full warm plans and optimizer iteration traces) would allow locating the update at which tip error and tip speed stopped decreasing inside the 0.05 s window.
